community.note: These values are estimates for 2020–2024 from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey. An unavailable value is not zero. Connecticut is unavailable because the survey uses planning regions, not the older counties this atlas uses.

datasets.title: Renter households spending 30%+ of income on gross rent
datasets.unit: percent of renter households whose share could be calculated
datasets.note: Renter households that pay 30% or more of their income for rent and utilities. The share leaves out households whose share the Census could not calculate. The site calculates this share, so there is no likely range.
datasets.geographyVintage: 2024 ACS counties; joined to Census 2021 atlas counties where FIPS match

datasets.title: Mean travel time to work (derived)
datasets.note: The average time to work for workers age 16 and older who do not work from home. The site calculates it from Census tables. It is not the Census's own published average. There is no likely range.
datasets.geographyVintage: 2024 ACS counties; joined to Census 2021 atlas counties where FIPS match

datasets.title: Median gross rent
datasets.note: The middle monthly rent for homes rented for cash. Rent includes utilities. County details show the margin of error (90%). Higher means more expensive. It is a cost, not a measure of quality.
datasets.geographyVintage: 2024 ACS counties; joined to Census 2021 atlas counties where FIPS match

datasets.title: Median home value
datasets.note: The middle value of homes that owners live in, as the owners estimate it. County details show the margin of error (90%). Higher means more expensive. It is a cost, not a measure of quality.
datasets.geographyVintage: 2024 ACS counties; joined to Census 2021 atlas counties where FIPS match

hazards.note: These are FEMA National Risk Index model estimates, version 1.20. They are not losses that happened. They do not predict a single year. The model uses data from different years for different hazards. FEMA's technical documents list them. Connecticut is unavailable because FEMA uses planning regions, not the older counties this atlas uses. This product uses FEMA's National Risk Index data but is not endorsed by FEMA. FEMA cannot vouch for analyses made after the data were retrieved.

healthcare.note: These are administrative shortage designations. The value is a priority score for placing clinicians. It is not a measured rate of the supply of providers. It is not a statement about one person's access to care.

datasets.title: Primary care shortage designation score
datasets.note: Some designations cover only part of a county. For those counties, the score describes that part. It does not describe the whole county. Counties with no current designation appear separately. That is not evidence of adequate access.

employment.note: The unemployment rate is the share of people in the labor force who have no job and look for one. The rate uses where people live, not where they work. It is not adjusted for seasons. The 2025 value is an average of 11 months, without October 2025. So it does not fully compare with other years. It is not a count of open jobs. It is not one person's chance of finding a job.

datasets.title: Unemployment rate
datasets.note: The unemployment rate is the share of people in the labor force who have no job and look for one. The rate uses where people live, not where they work. It is not adjusted for seasons. The 2025 value is an average of 11 months, without October 2025. So it does not fully compare with other years. It is not a count of open jobs. It is not one person's chance of finding a job.

broadband.note: The value is the share of residents with no reported access. It is 100% minus the reported access share. County details show the reported access share. A lower value is better. It is a county total, not a check of one address. It counts wired or fixed wireless broadband advertised at 100/20 Mbps or faster. Satellite does not count. The measurement is from June 2024. The FCC released it in 2025. It does not measure real speed, reliability, price or use. It is not a promise for one address. The source gives no resident counts and no likely range.

datasets.title: Residents without reported 100/20 Mbps access
datasets.note: The value is the share of residents with no reported access. It is 100% minus the reported access share. County details show the reported access share. A lower value is better. It is a county total, not a check of one address. It counts wired or fixed wireless broadband advertised at 100/20 Mbps or faster. Satellite does not count. The measurement is from June 2024. The FCC released it in 2025. It does not measure real speed, reliability, price or use. It is not a promise for one address. The source gives no resident counts and no likely range.

places.note: These are model estimates for adults from CDC PLACES, 2024 release. The model uses a 2022 CDC telephone health survey. The values are not direct counts. The CDC advises against using PLACES to rank the overall health of counties. The values are adjusted for age, so counties with older or younger people compare fairly. County details show the share before the age adjustment and the likely range (95%). The CDC does not endorse this atlas.

datasets.title: Current asthma among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they have asthma. These adults say they still have it. People report this themselves. Most differences between counties are smaller than the 95% likely range. Treat small gaps on this map as noise.

datasets.title: Diagnosed diabetes among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they have diabetes. This does not count diabetes only during pregnancy. The measure does not include diabetes that no one has found. So the true share is higher.

datasets.title: Frequent mental distress among adults
datasets.note: Adults who report 14 or more days of poor mental health in the past 30 days.

datasets.title: Obesity among adults
datasets.note: Adults with a body mass index of 30 or more. Body mass index comes from height and weight that people report themselves.

datasets.title: Current cigarette smoking among adults
datasets.note: Adults who have smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their life and now smoke every day or some days.

datasets.title: No leisure-time physical activity among adults
datasets.note: Adults who report no physical activity or exercise in the past month outside their regular job.

datasets.title: Binge drinking among adults
datasets.note: Men who report 5 or more drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days. Women who report 4 or more drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days.

datasets.title: Short sleep duration among adults
datasets.note: Adults who report usually sleeping less than 7 hours in a 24-hour period.

datasets.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, emphysema or chronic bronchitis.

datasets.title: Coronary heart disease among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they have angina or coronary heart disease.

datasets.title: Stroke among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they had a stroke.

datasets.title: Depression among adults
datasets.note: A health professional told these adults that they have a depressive disorder.

datasets.title: Fair or poor self-rated health among adults
datasets.note: Adults who rate their general health as fair or poor.

datasets.title: Frequent physical distress among adults
datasets.note: Adults who report 14 or more days of poor physical health in the past 30 days.

datasets.title: No health insurance among adults aged 18-64
datasets.note: Adults aged 18 to 64 who report no current health insurance coverage.

air.note: This measure is a model estimate of long-term fine particle pollution, known as PM2.5, where people live. The EPA Downscaler combines air monitors with an air quality model. Values are averages over 2020–2022. They are not daily air quality, smoke-event counts, or personal exposure. Source: CDC National Environmental Public Health Tracking Network. Interpretations here are not CDC's.

datasets.title: Fine particle pollution (PM2.5)
datasets.method: Mean of the 2020, 2021 and 2022 annual means of CDC's daily population-weighted county PM2.5 predictions (EPA Downscaler)
datasets.note: This value is the average for 2020, 2021 and 2022. Each year is an average of daily values, weighted to where people live. The unit is micrograms per cubic meter. Wildfire smoke can change a county's value a lot from year to year. County details show each year.

wildfire.note: This measure is a model estimate of wildfire risk from the USDA Forest Service. The value is a national rank for the county average. The scale runs from 0 to 100. The value is a rank, not a probability or a loss amount. Interpretations here are not the Forest Service's.

datasets.title: Wildfire risk to homes
datasets.method: National percentile rank of the county's mean Risk to Potential Structures, times 100
datasets.note: How the county's average wildfire risk to a home ranks among U.S. counties. Risk to homes combines wildfire likelihood and intensity with the general effect on a house. 100 is the highest risk.

datasets.title: Wildfire likelihood
datasets.method: National percentile rank of the county's mean annual burn probability, times 100
datasets.note: How the county's average chance of wildfire in a year ranks among U.S. counties. 100 is the highest likelihood.

water.note: This value is the share of people on community water systems. Their system had at least one health-based Safe Drinking Water Act violation in 2023–2025. One large system can decide a county's value. One violation of any length counts. Private wells are not covered. Interpretations here are not EPA's.

datasets.title: Drinking water health-based violations
datasets.unit: percent of people on community water systems
datasets.method: Population served by active community water systems with a health-based violation overlapping 2023–2025, divided by population served by all active community water systems listing the county, times 100
datasets.note: This value is the share of people on community water systems in the county. Their system had a health-based violation in 2023–2025. A violation can be a contaminant level, a treatment technique or a disinfectant limit. County details show the number of people and the number of systems.

traffic.note: These are deaths in motor vehicle crashes in the county per 100,000 residents a year for 2019–2023. The value describes how dangerous the county's roads are for everyone, including people passing through. It is not the risk for one resident. Small counties with busy highways can have very high values.

datasets.title: Traffic deaths
datasets.method: FARS deaths in crashes located in the county, 2019–2023, divided by 5 times the ACS 2019–2023 population, times 100,000
datasets.note: Five-year average of deaths in crashes on the county's public roads per 100,000 residents. County details show the death count and the number of residents.

climate.note: These climate normals come from NOAA observations on a grid. They describe typical past conditions across a county. They do not describe any one place in the county. They do not describe the future.

datasets.title: Days at or above 95°F
datasets.unit: days a year with a county-average high of 95°F or more
datasets.release: NOAA NCEI nClimGrid-Daily v1.0.0, scaled county averages
datasets.geographyVintage: NOAA county area averages; joined by FIPS through NOAA's state-code crosswalk
datasets.note: This value is the mean number of days a year from 1991–2020. On those days, the county's area-average daily high reached 95°F. NOAA estimates values between weather stations on a 5 km grid. It then averages the grid over the county. So this is a smoothed climate normal, not a thermometer reading. It hides urban heat islands and elevation differences within a county. The same 95°F means different things in humid and dry places. It is not a projection of future heat. Source: NOAA NCEI nClimGrid-Daily v1.0.0. NOAA does not endorse this atlas.

storms.note: These are storm reports to NOAA's Storm Events Database. More reports come in where more people live and watch. They are not a count of every storm, and they are not a forecast.

datasets.title: Tornado reports
datasets.unit: reports a year per 1,000 sq mi of land
datasets.release: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files v1.0
datasets.geographyVintage: NOAA county codes joined by FIPS to 2021 Census counties; land area from the 2021 Census Gazetteer
datasets.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Storm Events Database. https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/storm-events-database/
datasets.note: This value is the mean number of reports a year from 2006–2025, per 1,000 square miles of county land. Each report is one storm event in one county, as logged in NOAA's Storm Events Database. More reports come in where more people live and watch, so rural counties can read low. Winter, heat, high-wind and tropical storms are logged by forecast zone, not by county, so they are not counted here. Small independent cities have little land, so a few reports give a high rate. It is not a forecast. Source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database. NOAA does not endorse this atlas.

datasets.unit: reports a year per 1,000 sq mi of land
datasets.release: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files v1.0
datasets.geographyVintage: NOAA county codes joined by FIPS to 2021 Census counties; land area from the 2021 Census Gazetteer
datasets.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Storm Events Database. https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/storm-events-database/
datasets.note: This value is the mean number of reports a year from 2006–2025, per 1,000 square miles of county land. Each report is one storm event in one county, as logged in NOAA's Storm Events Database. More reports come in where more people live and watch, so rural counties can read low. Winter, heat, high-wind and tropical storms are logged by forecast zone, not by county, so they are not counted here. Small independent cities have little land, so a few reports give a high rate. It is not a forecast. Source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database. NOAA does not endorse this atlas.

crime.note: These are crimes reported to police and sent to the FBI. Not every crime is reported, and not every agency reports every month. The FBI advises against ranking places with these data.

datasets.title: Violent crime
datasets.release: FBI UCR Return A master files 2023–2025
datasets.geographyVintage: Agencies placed in their first FBI-listed county; 2021 Census counties
datasets.citation: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Return A master files, Crime Data Explorer. https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/
datasets.note: This value is crimes known to police per 100,000 residents, 2023–2025, from agencies that reported all 12 months. It counts reports, not all crime: many crimes are never reported. An agency counts fully in the first county the FBI lists for it, so a city that spans counties adds to one county only. A county is unavailable when its reporting agencies serve under 80% of its residents. The FBI advises against ranking places with these data. Source: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Return A. The FBI does not endorse this atlas.
